FOREWORD

0.1This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution

25 May 1971, after the draft finalized by the Shipbuilding Sectional Committee had been approved by the Marine, Cargo Movement and Packaging Division Council.

0.2 Snatch blocks for wire rope are used in various positions with the cargo handling gear and other general purpose work on ships. The blocks used on ships have to be tested to proof loads as specified in the Indian Dock Labourers Regulations, 1948, which is in accordance with the IL0 convention. 0.2.1 This standard and testing of cargo Societies. generally covers the regulations for the construction handling appliances specified by the Classification

0.2.2 Every ship has to carry a register of periodical examination and certificates of tests of all cargo gear in the forms prescribed under the Indian Dock Labourers Regulations, 1948. 0.2.3 Snatch blocks using wire ropes are permitted to be used only as deck lead blocks, or as span, blocks single or double reeved for topping In addition, they can also be used as lead blocks, the unloaded derrick. for guy tackle runners, if the runner is turned round to an angle of not more than 90". 0.3 In the preparation of this standard, considerable assistance has been derived from DIN 82220 ` Snatch blocks for wire ropes `, issued by Deutscher Normenausschuss ( Germany ). 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.
*Rules for rounding off numerical values ( reuised ).

3

IS : 6140- 1971 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard specifies the material, general dimensions and the test loads for the snatch blocks for use with wire ropes corresponding to the various working loads. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.0 For the purpose of this standard, the ~following definitions shall apply. 2.1 Snatch Blocks -A block with hinged strap to enable insertion of rope on to the sheave at any position on the length of a rope. 2.2 Cheeks The side plates fitted on either side of the sheave.

2.3 Safe Working Load-The maximum permissible load in tonnes for the rope of one of the single sheave blocks to take on one end. 2.4 Nominal Size-Safe nominal size of the block. 2.5 The names of various in figure in Table 1. 3. 6.1 Tolerance on certain dimensions are shown in the respective tables, The tolerance on other dimensions shall be coarse deviation according to IS : 2102-196911. 7. TESTING 7.1 The snatch block as a whole shall be tested to a proof load of four The test load shall be maintimes the safe working load of the block. tained for a period of five minutes. 7.2 At the end of the test, the blocks shall be opened and all parts examined for permanent deformation or other defects. The blocks shall be approved subject to there being no permanent deformation or other defects on any of their parts.

8. MARKING 8.1 All snatch blocks shall be marked
with the following: a) Proof load in tonnes, b) Nominal size ( safe working authority's load in tonnes ), seal with date of test, and mark. with the IS1 Certification on the strap in an indelible manner

c) The inspecting
8.1.1 Mark. The snatch

d) The manufacturer's

identification

blocks may also be marked

NOTE- The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act, and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. Presence of this mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard, under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control during production. This system, which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer, has the further safeguard that the products .as actually marketed are continuously checked by ISI for conformity to the Standard. Details of conditions, under which a licence for the use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.
